$comment: THE CERTIFIED RELEASE LINEAGE OF THIS PACK. WHY IT LIVES IN scripts/ RATHER THAN artifacts/, where this repository keeps its other reviewed records: the evaluator consults it to decide an outcome, so it has to sit inside the release-material boundary — a record that decides eligibility from outside the verified material could be edited without the verification noticing, which is the shape of the defect FE-13 removes. It cannot be added to that boundary as a new artifacts/ entry, because MATERIAL is versioned with the release: `materialise` requires every declared path to be present, so widening the list retroactively makes every release predating the new entry unmaterialisable. That is the same fact ADR 0008 records in another costume, and this file is placed rather than the boundary widened. Each entry records the immutable Git object a released version of these standards designates, as a fact that can be checked rather than a name that can be reused. It exists because `refs/tags/v1.0.0` is only a name: any repository can create an annotated tag of that spelling pointing at any commit, so a check that merely finds the tag proves the spelling and nothing else. Comparing against the oid recorded here is what makes the lineage a fact about this pack. WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR: establishing eligibility for the self-maintenance mode of `standards maintain` (FE-13, ADR 0009) — it says which history a working tree must descend from before it may be treated as this pack maintaining itself. WHAT IT IS NOT: it is not an attestation, it records no human judgement, and it confers no compliance on anything. A maintainer adds a row at release time, after the tag exists, by reading the tag; the value is verifiable by anyone with the repository and is wrong or right rather than reviewed. It is never regenerated by a run. KNOWN LIMIT, stated here because the file would otherwise imply more than it delivers: a fork of this repository possesses this file and the tag it names, so this establishes lineage membership, not exclusivity. ADR 0009 carries that argument and the reason it is bounded rather than closed.

1.0.0.$note: The 1.0.0 release. Certified against 9809afc by an independent pass recorded in artifacts/release-review/. It predates the FE-13 release-identity mechanism and cannot claim it (ADR 0008).
1.0.0.$signingNote: Unsigned. It predates the SSH release-signing regime (ADR 0010) and cannot acquire it retroactively (ADR 0008). Recorded as a fact about the release rather than left absent, so that a consumer reads "not signed under this regime" instead of inferring either unsigned-therefore-fine or unsigned-therefore-broken.

1.1.0.$note: The first release signed under the regime ADR 0010 established. Certified before publication by ci/certify-release.mjs (R2) against the tag while it was still unpushed; the evidence block is in artifacts/evidence/2026-08-26-v1.1.0-release-ceremony.md. The signer fingerprint is recorded so a reader can check which identity authorised this release without consulting the trust store, but it is NOT the trust anchor: the authoritative public key lives in the operator trust store outside every pack (ADR 0013), and a fingerprint copied into the pack could be replaced by a fork along with everything else.
